system.name: Recipe sharing web app
system.description: Users publish recipes, browse, comment, and upload photos

assumptions.text: 30% of registered users are daily active
2 sessions per active user per day
10x peak factor from single-timezone evening concentration

components.name: Application instance
components.justification: 0.28 peak RPS against a single instance's capacity leaves roughly four orders of magnitude of headroom.

components.name: Managed relational database
components.justification: 0.66 GB/year on the smallest tier. Managed for tested point-in-time recovery, which a two-person team will not build or exercise themselves.

components.name: Object storage for photos
components.justification: 13 GB/year of photos. Serving binaries from the application instance would couple storage growth to compute.

components.name: CDN / edge cache
components.justification: Photo-heavy payloads at 30 KB average; a free tier removes egress from the single instance at no cost.

rejected_components.reason: Three times the complexity budget and four times the money budget for a system with four orders of magnitude of headroom on one instance.
rejected_components.revisit_when: More than 4 independently deployable services exist and a dedicated operations engineer is on the team.

rejected_components.reason: At 0.24 peak reads/second there is no measured read pressure to relieve.
rejected_components.revisit_when: A single query exceeds 10 requests/second at over 50 ms, or database CPU is sustained above 60% for 3 days.

rejected_components.reason: 0.042 writes/second. A broker solves a throughput problem five orders of magnitude beyond measured demand.
rejected_components.revisit_when: Sustained above 500 events/second, or 3 or more independent consumer groups need to replay the same stream.

rejected_components.reason: The primary is idle at this load; a replica would add a component and replication lag for no measured benefit.
rejected_components.revisit_when: Database CPU sustained above 70% for 3 days after query optimisation.

rejected_components.reason: Full-text search in the existing relational database satisfies the browse and search requirement at this catalogue size.
rejected_components.revisit_when: Search p95 exceeds 300 ms, or ranking requirements exceed what the database provides.

options.description: One application instance, managed database, object storage, CDN
trade_offs: Single instance means restarts are visible to users
Realistically about 99.5% availability, which is not claimed as more
No complexity headroom left: adding anything requires removing something

options.description: One instance with a file-based database on a persistent volume
options.reason: No managed point-in-time recovery. Restore is manual and untested, and a two-person team will not exercise it. GBP 15/month buys a tested recovery path.

options.description: The selected option plus a cache and a read replica
options.reason: Over the complexity budget (6 > 4) and over the money budget. At 0.28 peak RPS neither component has a problem to solve.
trade_offs: Would absorb a sudden traffic increase without redesign

availability.explanation: No availability target was stated, so none is claimed. A single instance with platform restarts and managed database maintenance windows realistically delivers about 99.5%. 99.9% would require a different architecture and budget.

open_questions: Is there a regulatory or data-residency constraint not mentioned?
Is photo upload volume closer to 20% of writes, or higher?
